BMI_Clinical_Note: BMI <18.5 — Energy & protein repletion required. High nutritional risk.
Hormone_Therapy: No Hormone Therapy (TNBC — ER-, PR-, HER2-)
Bone_Density_Concern: MODERATE — Post-menopausal bone loss. DEXA screening. Calcium + Vit D + weight-bearing exercise.
Nutrition_Impact_Symptoms: Constipation; Dry Mouth; Fatigue; Skin Reaction/Radiation Dermatitis
Zinc_mg_per_day: 10 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — important for immune function + wound healing
Dietary_Fibre_g_per_day: 40 g/day (ICMR-NIN 2020); reduce to 25 g if diarrhoea/mucositis
Omega3_Recommendation: Dietary omega-3: mustard oil cooking + flaxseed + walnuts + fatty fish (if non-veg) 2x/week
Protein_Source_Note: Vegetarian protein: dal+rice combo (complete AA), paneer, curd, soya, moong, rajma, chickpeas, tofu, amaranth
Alcohol_Guidance: ZERO alcohol — carcinogen; increases BC recurrence risk [ESPEN C5-2]
ICMR_NIN_2020_Reference: ICMR-NIN Nutrient Requirements & RDA for Indians (2020 revision)
Nutrition_Route_ESPEN: Individualized dietary counselling + ONS → EN if goals not met [ESPEN B3-1]
Supplement_Recommendation: ONS 1–2x/day: Pentasure HP / Ensure Plus / Fresubin Energy / Disprolene (Indian brands preferred); Calcium 600–1000 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) + Vitamin D 400–800 IU/day — endemic Vit D deficiency in India; Vitamin B12 1–2 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) or 500 mcg/week cyanocobalamin — B12 deficiency common in Indian vegetarians; Algae-based DHA 200–500 mg/day (omega-3 for vegetarian Indian BC patients); Iron 19–29 mg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020) — monitor Hb; IV iron if <8 g/dL on chemo; Folate 220–400 mcg/day (ICMR-NIN 2020; higher during chemo); Ground flaxseed 1–2 tbsp/day (lignans — phytoestrogen modulation; beneficial ER+ Indian BC survivors); Multivitamin/mineral at RDA dose ONLY (ICMR-NIN 2020). NOT high-dose. Avoid selenium, Vit E, Vit C megadoses during chemo.
Exercise_Plan_ESPEN_India: Aerobic: Brisk walk 45 min/day OR 150–300 min/week (cycling, swimming, Zumba, yoga) [ESPEN B4-1/C5-1]; Resistance: 2–3x/week, 8–12 reps, major muscle groups; can use resistance bands/body weight at home [ESPEN B4-2]; Yoga: 3–5x/week (Suryanamaskar, Pranayama, Shavasana) — evidence for fatigue reduction + cortisol in Indian BC survivors; TARGET: 150–300 min/week moderate activity — reduces Indian BC recurrence risk and improves overall survival
ESPEN_Guidelines_India: 📋 SCREENING [B1-1]: Regular nutritional assessment from diagnosis. Indian BC patients — ICMR/WHO Asian BMI cut-offs apply (Normal: 18.5–22.9; Overweight: ≥23; Obese: ≥25). [East India (West Bengal/Odisha/Bihar/Jharkhand)] | 📋 ASSESSMENT [B1-2]: PG-SGA score elevated → quantitative assessment: 24-hr dietary recall, muscle mass (BIA/DEXA/mid-arm circumference), grip strength, CRP/albumin, NIS. | ⚡ ENERGY [B2-1]: 25–30 kcal/kg/day (ESPEN). Indian context: average Indian BC woman body weight 55–65 kg. Total: 1400–2000 kcal/day depending on stage and activity. | 🥩 PROTEIN [B2-2]: >1 g/kg/day (ESPEN); ICMR-NIN 2020 RDA: 0.83 g/kg/day (healthy); BC treatment: 1.0–1.5 g/kg/day. Vegetarian patients: dal+rice+dairy combination essential for complete amino acid profile. | 💊 MICRONUTRIENTS [B2-4 + ICMR-NIN 2020]: Vitamin D (endemic deficiency in India — 400–1000 IU/day), Calcium (600–1200 mg/day from ragi/dairy/sesame), Iron (19–29 mg/day), Folate (220–400 mcg/day). AVOID high-dose antioxidants during chemo. | 🥗 NUTRITION [B3-1]: Active nutritional counselling + ONS if enriched Indian diet insufficient. | ⚠ INTERVENTION [B3-2]: No energy restriction during treatment. No unproven diets — ketogenic, prolonged fasting, 'cancer-curing' diets widely promoted on Indian social media are NOT evidence-based. | 🔪 SURGERY [C1-1/C1-3]: ERAS protocol. Screen pre-operatively. Post-op: oral diet day 1 if tolerated. Protein 1.2–1.5 g/kg/day for wound healing/reconstruction. Indian foods: moong dal khichdi → dal-rice → normal diet progression. | ☢ RADIOTHERAPY [C2-1]: Breast RT — maintain adequate protein + Vit C + Zinc for skin healing. Skin nutrition important for Indian patients with darker skin (higher radiation dermatitis risk in some studies). | 🔴 TNBC [Indian]: High incidence in young premenopausal Indian women. Aggressive chemo → highest nutritional risk. Protein priority 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day. Anti-inflammatory diet. Immunotherapy GI AE management. | 🏃 SURVIVOR [C5-1/C5-2]: Regular PA strongly recommended — 150–300 min/week. Mediterranean-Indian hybrid diet. ZERO alcohol. Maintain BMI 18.5–22.9 (Indian cut-offs). Yoga beneficial for Indian survivors. | 🏋 EXERCISE [B4-1/B4-2]: Aerobic + resistance training recommended. Yoga as adjunct for Indian patients (evidence for fatigue, QoL, cortisol reduction). Lymphedema: progressive resistance IS SAFE. | ❌ BEWARE: High-dose supplement marketing targeting Indian cancer patients (social media/WhatsApp) — vitamin megadoses, 'cancer-curing' supplements, unproven herbal products — not recommended without oncologist approval [ESPEN B2-4].
Diet_Chart_Indian_Meal_Plan: 🌅 Breakfast: Upma (semolina/suji, small portion) + mixed vegetables + peanuts + 1 boiled egg (eggetarian/NV) / extra dal + herbal tea || 🕙 Mid-Morning: Coconut water (1 glass, electrolytes) + 1 banana + 5 almonds (Vit E) || 🍽 Lunch: Khichdi (brown rice + moong dal, 1.5 cups) with ghee (1 tsp) + mixed vegetable raita + papad + beetroot salad | Comfort + complete protein || 🕓 Snack: Prunes/anjeer (3) + 1 glass warm jeera-saunf water + flaxseed chutney (1 tsp); walk 15 min after; psyllium husk (isabgol, 1 tsp) in water if needed || 🌙 Dinner: Khichdi (rice + moong, 1.5 cups, light ghee) + mixed vegetable raita + roasted papad | Easily digestible + complete protein || 🌛 Bedtime: Warm jeera (cumin) water + 1 small cup dahi (probiotic — gut microbiome) | Avoid if hot flashes disturb sleep || 🌿 SOY NOTE: 1–2 servings/day of desi soy foods (soya chunks/tofu/soy milk) SAFE and beneficial for ER+ Indian BC survivors. Phytoestrogens do NOT act like estrogen. High-dose soy supplements — avoid. || Regional: Include fish curry (omega-3) 2–3x/week for NV patients; prefer hand-pounded/red rice over polished white; dal-bhaat-sabzi as base; mustard oil (omega-3 source). || 💰 Middle SES: Balanced home-cooking. Weekly fish/egg 2–3x. Millet rotation. Seasonal produce. Avoid processed/packaged foods marketed as 'healthy'. || ✅ UNDERWEIGHT: Fortify ALL Indian meals: add ghee/coconut oil (1 tsp extra), milk powder (2 tbsp) to dalia/oats, peanut chutney, til laddoo, dry fruits. Commercial ONS 2x/day. Target +0.5 kg/week. Khova/mawa laddoo or high-calorie kheer if well tolerated. || 🌱 VEGETARIAN BC PATIENT: Complete protein strategy — dal+rice/roti at same meal (complementary AA), include rajma/chana/lentils daily, paneer/tofu/soya 1–2x/day, dahi 1–2 cups/day, sprouted legumes. B12 supplement if vegan. Omega-3: flaxseed + walnuts + algae-based DHA supplement. || 🔴 TNBC (Indian): Higher prevalence in young Indian women (<40 yrs). Highest metabolic demand. Protein 1.5–2.0 g/kg/day mandatory during chemo. Anti-inflammatory diet: haldi, adrak, omega-3, berries, green tea. Immunotherapy patients: watch for immune-related colitis — low-residue if GI symptoms. || ❌ STRICTLY AVOID [ALL INDIAN BC PATIENTS]: Alcohol, tobacco (paan/gutka), vanaspati/dalda (trans fats), excess ghee in obese patients, maida/refined flour products, packaged namkeen/biscuits, sugar-sweetened drinks (even fruit juice), raw/undercooked meat/eggs during chemo. || 🐟 OMEGA-3 FOR VEGETARIANS: Ground flaxseed (1–2 tbsp/day) + walnuts (5–7/day) + mustard oil for cooking + algae-based DHA supplement (250–500 mg/day) — essential since no fish intake. || 🏃 YOGA + EXERCISE [ESPEN B4-1/B4-2]: Brisk walk 45 min/day + yoga (reduces cortisol/fatigue, improves QoL in Indian BC survivors) + resistance 2–3x/week. Reduces BC recurrence risk significantly.
